title: Permission conformance harness and audit-replay bench
creator: Aisha Carter
description: Build a repeatable conformance and regression bench for RBAC v2 permissions that ties deterministic audit log replays to permission snapshots. This ticket establishes the harness, canonical fixtures, mutation corpus, and CI orchestration required to validate policy changes across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Goal: catch permission regressions, SAML/SSO mapping errors, and audit-logging discrepancies before rollout.
background: Recent permission regressions surfaced in a canary rollout where a subtle role-mapping change allowed read access to internal metrics. Current golden fixture tests are fragmented: some live in unit tests, others in ad-hoc scripts. We need a single bench that can: 1) load canonical access-state snapshots (users, teams, roles, resources), 2) run deterministic request sequences against policy evaluation and service endpoints, 3) replay audit logs to assert that emitted events match expected attributes (actor, action, resource, result), and 4) run mutation and fuzz scenarios representative of SAML attribute mappings and token expirations.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can load and apply a canonical access snapshot and bring the policy evaluator to a known state
Deterministic replay of recorded request sequences produces identical policy decisions across environment variants (hosted/dedicated/private)
Audit log replayer validates event content and ordering; mismatches produce a clear diff artifact uploaded to CI
Mutation corpus (role rename, attribute mismatch, expired session, delegated tokens) runs in CI and flags regressions
Bench integrates with existing CI to block merges when priority regressions are detected
Documentation for creating new canonical fixtures and adding replay scenarios published in Confluence
steps_to_run_locally: checkout rbac-tests repo and runtime integration branch
brew install redis postgresql (or use docker-compose included)

2025-02-03: Discovered non-determinism in distributed token service when replaying high-concurrency sequences; added deterministic token-supply shim for bench runs.

2025-02-15: CI integration spike completed: feature branch now emits artifacts (audit diffs) as pipeline artifacts and fails if a high-severity mismatch is found. Next: harden fixture coverage and run across private deployment smoke matrix.
notes: Keep fixtures compact: prefer representative resource sets (~150 resources) with parameterized templates to generate larger permutations. Coordinate with SRE to provision a replay-friendly staging topology (time warp, deterministic caches).
